problem: "Network operators supply SIMs, NB-IoT, LoRaWAN or Wi-Fi backhaul" mixes up local links and backhaul. Wi-Fi is a short-range local link, not backhaul, and mobile operators do not normally supply it; LoRaWAN is often run privately by an enterprise rather than a telecom operator, so a student may think all four are the same kind of operator service.
fix: Write: "Network operators supply cellular connectivity — SIMs, NB-IoT or 4G/5G — and sometimes LoRaWAN; Wi-Fi is usually a local link or backhaul provided by the site owner, not the mobile operator."

problem: "XaaS, everything as a service" is a loose expansion. The usual expansion is "anything as a service", and the sentence reads as if XaaS means only the full outcome bundle.
fix: Write: "XaaS (anything as a service) is the general name for selling a capability as a recurring service; in IoT the full outcome — monitoring, analytics, maintenance and reports as a monthly service, not a box — is one such case."

problem: "Chapter 1.7 contrasts this with IoT" is a plain-text cross-reference; series convention is a link to the other chapter, and as written the reader on a phone cannot jump to it.
fix: Make it a link to the M2M chapter, e.g. the M2M chapter contrasts this with IoT, or drop the sentence and let Section 1 carry the contrast.
